home.lead: Glycosearch explores glycoscience research, from the cell-surface glycocalyx and cell-penetrating peptides to bioorthogonal labeling and data science. Discover publications, research tools and an interactive learning playground.
home.intro: How glycans are drawn and written, what glycome and glycomics mean, and how sugars are labelled in living cells.

themes.title: Glycocalyx and glycosaminoglycans in cellular uptake
themes.text: Cells are covered by a layer of negatively charged oligo- and polysaccharides. This work asks how heparan sulfate and other glycosaminoglycans take part in the uptake of cell-penetrating peptides and drug delivery vectors — and where binding does not translate into uptake.

themes.title: Peptide uptake and cytosolic delivery
themes.text: Designing cell-penetrating peptides and measuring where they end up: short hydrophobic peptides identified by rational design, the cell uptake and membrane binding of lactam-stapled peptides, and a GFP complementation assay that detects cytosolic import.

themes.title: Bioorthogonal labeling with BCN (SPAAC)
themes.text: Bicyclo[6.1.0]nonyne probes for copper-free, strain-promoted alkyne–azide cycloaddition, applied to the labeling and three-dimensional imaging of living cells.

themes.title: Cell migration and tumour glycobiology
themes.text: Adhesion mechanisms in interstitial cell migration, the glycocalyx as an integrin-independent adhesion system, and the role of highly sulfated chondroitin sulfate in ovarian carcinoma.

themes.title: Glycosylation disorders
themes.text: A clinical and biochemical study of deficient CMP-sialic acid transport.

themes.title: Biomaterials and biolubricants
themes.text: How the surface stress of biomedical silicones acts as a stimulant of cellular response, and how recombinant lubricin analogs can be manufactured as biolubricants.

themes.title: Data science for functional genomics
themes.text: Retrospective re-analyses of published data: how guide selection carries over between noncanonical ORF screens, and when microprotein sequence scores transfer between assays.

themes.title: Open research software
themes.text: Web applications and R packages that accompany the research: Frapbot for FRAP data, Peptify, and four Google Summer of Code projects.

glossary.text: The glycome is the entire complement of sugars, whether free or present in more complex molecules, of an organism.
Glycomics is the study of the role of carbohydrates & carbohydrate-containing biomolecules in biological systems.

Copper-free bioorthogonal cycloaddition of a cyclooctyne with an organic azide, leading to the formation of a stable 1,2,3-triazole. Among other applications, SPAAC is used for the detection of biomolecules, e.g. sialic acids.

nomenclatureText.symbol: The symbol nomenclature is based on criteria defined by editors of the textbook 'Essentials of Glycobiology' and have to be convenient for the annotation of mass spectra.
nomenclatureText.text: The text nomenclature comprises the anomeric carbon next to the correct abbreviation of the corresponding glycan. Including the anomeric carbon is important, and is likely to become increasingly more so in the future as more complicated structures are discovered. The presence of parentheses (which then necessitates the use of brackets to indicate branching structures) is unnecessarily cumbersome, particularly when representing the structure in 2D form.
nomenclatureText.combined: Examples of symbol nomenclature used to illustrate N- and O-linked glycans written in the 2D version of the text nomenclature. Note that symbol structures will be used to annotate data where linkages have not been defined (e.g MALDI profiling), and if linkages between monosaccharides are known, they can be added above or to the side of the line connecting the symbols if desired (e.g. alpha6 or beta4).

profile.name: Dr. Samuel Schmidt
career: I am a researcher in biochemistry and molecular biology and the Co-Founder, CFO, Product Lead and Data Scientist of Vaionex Corporation, an AI and blockchain development and data science company.

At Vaionex, I oversee the financial, legal and operational side of the company and contribute to product strategy, product development, and AI and data science solutions, including the contract platform Agreements.ai. In my recent data science work with Robin Gounder, I re-analyze published functional genomics data on noncanonical open reading frames and microproteins.

My scientific background is in glycobiology. I completed my experimental Ph.D. thesis in the group of Prof. Dr. Peter Friedl at the Department of Cell Biology, Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences (RIMLS) in Nijmegen, The Netherlands. The thesis examined the impact of cell-surface glycosylation on tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and in vivo, using multiphoton, confocal and scanning electron microscopy to visualize the complex nanotopography between cell membranes and collagen fibers.

In 2013, I was awarded the Roche Postdoc Fellowship (RPF) by F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd, Basel, Switzerland. In the group of Prof. Dr. Roland Brock at the Department of Biochemistry, RIMLS, I developed a GFP complementation assay to study the transport of functional cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) from the cell surface to the cytosol, with a focus on endosomal release. I also studied the influence of cell-surface glycosylation on the uptake of CPPs.
In February 2017, I was awarded the KIC Postdoc Fellowship by the Kavli Institute at Cornell for Nanoscale Science, Cornell University, USA, where I was a KIC PostDoc Fellow from 2018 to 2022.

experience.where: Kavli Institute at Cornell for Nanoscale Science and Robert Frederick Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA
experience.text: As a Kavli Fellow, I investigated how specific biophysical and biochemical properties of the cell-surface glycan layer (the glycocalyx) enable cells to interact with nanometer-scale structures in biological tissues and biomimetic culture systems.

experience.where: Biochemistry of Integrated Systems, RIMLS, Nijmegen, The Netherlands
experience.text: In this project, I developed a GFP complementation assay to study the transport of functional cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) from the cell surface to the cytosol, with a focus on endosomal release. I also studied the influence of cell-surface glycosylation on the uptake of CPPs. Alongside advanced biochemical approaches, fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP), I used confocal microscopy to analyze and visualize the contact regions between CPPs (especially cationic CPPs) and negatively charged cell-surface glycan moieties. Furthermore, I studied the impact of CPP binding on the lateral mobility of cell-surface glycolipids and glycoproteins using atomic force microscopy and spectroscopy (AFM/AFS) and the FRAP technique, which I have optimized for glycan analysis over the past years.

experience.where: Cellbiology and Celldynamics, RIMLS, Nijmegen, The Netherlands
experience.text: During my Ph.D. project, I was able to learn advanced imaging procedures, including confocal microscopy, to visualize cell-matrix interactions and dynamic cell patterning, for example during tumor migration and invasion. My responsibilities included developing a cell culture technique to analyze the influence of glycocalyx components in mediating cell migration and invasion in a 3D environment in vitro and in vivo. As a result, I have a strong background in cell and molecular biology and in microscopy, including time-lapse microscopy, confocal microscopy, and atomic force microscopy and spectroscopy (AFM/AFS), as well as in glycobiology, and I have experience in glycochemistry.
